name: China economy
summary: China's October output rose 4.8% and retail sales 0.4%, below forecasts, while fixed-asset investment kept falling
state: Statistics bureau data of 16 Nov showed October industrial output up 4.8% on a year and retail sales up 0.4%, both below expectations, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% and property investment fell sharply in January–October (NBS; CGTN). The bureau described the economy as generally stable. Searches on 19 Nov found no new developer default wave, financial contagion or tightened capital controls, so Normal holds with momentum weakening.
for_you: Weaker Chinese demand tends to weigh on commodity exporters and firms selling into China, and can push down prices of goods China exports. No direct effect on UK households has been reported.
rubric_hit: Normal: growth near target, no financial contagion; output +4.8% y/y in Oct, well above 3% hard-landing line

sources.title: National Bureau of Statistics of China — National economy was generally stable in October
CGTN — China's Jan–Oct economy remains stable, says NBS

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
